title: 2011 Reno Air Races crash
summary: During the third lap of the National Championship Air Races unlimited class gold race at Reno/Stead Airport, a modified North American P-51D (Race 177, The Galloping Ghost) experienced a left roll upset and high-G pitch-up at 445 knots near pylon 8. The upset exceeded the structural limits of the elevator trim tab system, which had been weakened by loosened attachment screws and a fatigue crack. The left elevator trim tab separated in flight, causing loss of control. The pilot became incapacitated from high G-forces, and the aircraft descended onto the airport ramp in the spectator box seating area, killing the pilot and 10 spectators.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board determines that the probable cause of this accident was the reduced stiffness of the elevator trim tab system that allowed aerodynamic flutter to occur at racing speeds. The reduced stiffness was a result of deteriorated locknut inserts that allowed the trim tab attachment screws to become loose and to initiate fatigue cracking in one screw sometime before the accident flight. Aerodynamic flutter of the trim tabs resulted in a failure of the left trim tab link assembly, elevator movement, high flight loads, and a loss of control. Contributing to the accident were the undocumented and untested major modifications to the airplane and the pilot's operation of the airplane in the unique air racing environment without adequate flight testing.

factors.evidence: Aerodynamic flutter of elevator trim tabs occurred at racing speed of 445 knots, caused by reduced structural stiffness (p. 2, 30-31). Loosened attachment screws and deteriorated locknut inserts allowed flutter to develop.

Elevator trim tab attachment screws had loose connections and a fatigue crack developed in one screw. Deteriorated locknut inserts rendered them ineffective at providing clamping pressure to keep hinge surfaces tight (p. 1, 43).

Undocumented and untested major modifications to aircraft, including single controllable elevator trim tab (increased aerodynamic load), filler material on trim tabs (increased weight and moved CG aft), and elevator counterweight modifications (p. 2). No engineering evaluations or flight testing for modifications (p. 1).

Failure of left elevator trim tab link assembly due to dynamic compressive loads exceeding buckling strength, caused by flutter excitation (p. 1). Right elevator trim tab also showed failure of its fixed link assembly (p. 1).

During upset, vertical acceleration peaked at 17.3 G, airplane rolled from 73° left bank to 93° left bank in less than 1 second, then entered right-rolling climb (p. 2). Pilot likely experienced G-induced loss of consciousness within 1 second (p. 2).

Aircraft descended in helical flightpath and collided with airport ramp in spectator box seating area at approximately 1625 PDT, killing 1 pilot and 10 spectators, injuring at least 64 people on ground (p. 2).

events.text: National Championship Air Races unlimited class gold race underway at Reno/Stead Airport. Aircraft in third place, about 4.5 seconds behind Voodoo, 8.8 seconds behind Strega.
Aircraft approaching pylon 8 during third lap of six-lap race
Aircraft rounding pylon 8 at 445 knots in established left-bank turn
LEFT ROLL UPSET BEGINS: Aircraft rapidly rolls from 73° left bank toward 93° left bank; vertical acceleration reaches 11 G during upset
Aircraft rolling right and pitching up; reaches maximum vertical load factor; elevator trim tab link assembly experiencing peak dynamic compressive loads
Aircraft pitching up with left elevator trim tab at trailing edge down position, right trim tab trailing edge up, full right-wing-down aileron deflection
LEFT ELEVATOR TRIM TAB SEPARATES IN FLIGHT; inboard piece detached from hinges
COLLISION: Aircraft descends in helical flightpath and strikes airport ramp in spectator box seating area; fragments upon impact

recommendations.text: Require engineering evaluations and flutter analysis for aircraft with major modifications before race eligibility
Require flight testing and certification of modified racing aircraft flight characteristics
Issue guidance on spectator safety distances and safety areas for air races
Provide high-G training requirements for air race pilots and evaluate G-suit feasibility

safety_changes: NTSB issued 10 safety recommendations on April 10, 2012 to RARA, NAG, and FAA addressing air race safety
Focus on engineering evaluations for aircraft with major modifications, spectator safety, course design guidance, and high-G training
